extracted.intended_audience: founders, startup PRs, communications professionals, journalists-interested-in-PR-ethics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for ethical public relations and press outreach aimed at founders and PR practitioners; contrasts manipulative tactics with honest practices and a quality rubric for PR work.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Media Manipulation Cycle (Critical View)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade media (small, specialized) covers a story → mid-tier media picks it up to amplify → top-tier media validates it as 'news' → story shapes public discourse regardless of accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand how stories can be deliberately seeded and amplified; use this knowledge to avoid intentionally gaming small outlets to bait larger ones. Recognize that amplification does not equal factual validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real news, not manufactured
rubrics_metrics.description: PR should present actual newsworthy events or developments rather than plant stories or fabricate events for attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid planting fake stories in small outlets to bait larger ones, manufactured controversies, or converting advertorial content into 'news.' Quality rubric repeats: 'Real news, not manufactured.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest framing throughout
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative and pitch should be framed truthfully without deceptive spin or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid emotional manipulation tactics and pitches that are not real news; honest framing is emphasized in the manifesto and quality rubric. Honest framing builds long-term reputation; manipulative framing may work short-term but fails long-term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiable claims with methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims made in PR must be verifiable and, where applicable, accompanied by methodology or evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data, methods, or supporting documentation so reporters can verify claims. The page advises 'verifiable claims with methodology' as part of honest PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named sources with clear stakes disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer named sources and disclose their interests/stakes rather than relying on anonymous or strategically leaked sourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named sources with credentials should be provided; anonymous sources are often strategic leaks and can be manipulative. 'Named sources with clear stakes disclosed' appears in multiple lists as required practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: PR materials should acknowledge the limitations or caveats of claims or products rather than overclaiming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly disclose scope and limitations to avoid misleading reporters/readers; 'acknowledgment of limitations' is listed under 'What Honest PR Looks Like.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor embargoes religiously
rubrics_metrics.description: If an embargo is negotiated, it must be respected by the party offering it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not burn embargoes for convenience; avoid offering embargoes without actual exclusivity. The manifesto says 'Honor embargoes religiously' and reporters list burning embargoes as a grievance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Any conflicts of interest related to spokespeople, sources, or story sponsors must be clearly disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters object to hidden spokesperson conflicts. The Honest PR Manifesto and quality rubric both call for disclosure of conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make sources genuinely available
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that sources promised to reporters are actually accessible for comment and verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manifesto: 'Make sources genuinely available.' Avoid strategic 'anonymous sources' or promised spokespeople who are unreachable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term relationships over short-term wins
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize building sustained relationships with journalists and audiences rather than seeking one-off attention through manipulative tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term reputation is framed as the most valuable asset; manipulative tactics may yield short-term coverage but harm relationships and reputation over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect journalists' time
rubrics_metrics.description: Founders and PRs should be responsible and considerate in interactions with journalists, avoiding frivolous or non-news pitches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pitch stories that aren't real news, avoid repetitive inappropriate pitching, and avoid wasting reporters' time with token access or unverified claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not plant fake stories in small outlets to bait larger ones
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid deliberately seeding false or fabricated stories in niche/trade outlets with the expectation they'll be amplified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'Tactics to Avoid' — planting fake stories is a manipulative technique Holiday exposes; it undermines credibility and is unethical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use anonymous sources to attack competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid leveraging anonymous sourcing to initiate attacks or smear competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page warns that anonymous sources are frequently strategic leaks and can be used to unfairly harm others; reporters dislike this practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not manufacture controversies for attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Refrain from creating or inflating controversies solely to attract media attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufactured controversies are listed among tactics to avoid; they may generate short-term traffic but damage trust and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not offer embargoes without actual exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not promise exclusivity via embargo if no real exclusivity exists or will be honored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering false embargoes is manipulative and is explicitly listed as a tactic to avoid; it also violates the manifesto's requirement to 'Honor embargoes religiously.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pass advertorial content as news
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly distinguish sponsored/advertorial content from editorial news; do not present advertorial material as independent news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'News' that's actually advertorial content is flagged as a manipulative practice to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid emotional manipulation tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on emotionally manipulative language or approaches designed to provoke a disproportionate reaction for coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters list 'using emotional manipulation tactics' as a complaint; honest PR should be factual and measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not hide spokesperson conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not conceal relationships, financial interests, or other conflicts tied to spokespeople quoted or cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hiding conflicts is a repeated reporter grievance and runs counter to the manifesto’s call to disclose conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pitch the same 'exclusive' to multiple outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not simultaneously promise exclusivity to multiple journalists or outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters explicitly list pitching the same 'exclusive' to multiple outlets as a bad practice; it undermines trust and damages relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the truth, even when uncomfortable
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to full honesty in PR communications, including admitting unfavorable facts when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 'Honest PR Manifesto' — truthfulness is presented as a core ethical obligation and foundation for sustainable reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric (Ethical PR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A succinct checklist summarizing ethical PR: Real news, not manufactured; Honest framing; Conflicts disclosed; Named sources with credentials; Embargoes honored; Long-term reputation focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist as an evaluative quick-reference when preparing press materials or judging PR conduct; it aggregates the page's main standards.
